title: Lesson 30: General Systems Architecture: Testing AI Systems: Evals, Golden Sets, Canaries, and Regression
description: The testing discipline AI systems demand in place of the unit test: evals as structured tests, golden sets as the regression anchor, and canaries as the production safety net.

questions.question: Per the lesson “General Systems Architecture: Testing AI Systems: Evals, Golden Sets, Canaries, and Regression”, an eval suite is deliberately aimed at problems the agent still fails about half the time. Why can it not answer whether a change broke something?
options: Because LLM-as-a-judge graders are nondeterministic and cannot be calibrated against human graders.
Because the suite runs offline rather than against live production traffic.
Because that is a capability eval, and the regression question needs its own suite with a near-100% expected pass rate.
Because a golden set has to be rebuilt from scratch on every deployment.
questions.explanation: Capability evals are a hill to climb with a low expected pass rate, and a score change on them says nothing about whether an existing behavior regressed.

questions.question: Which statement best reflects the lesson’s guidance?
options: A canary that watches only error rate and latency is a software canary wearing an AI costume; hallucination rate, coherence, LLM-as-a-judge results, and business signals belong from the first stage.
Canary routing should be random per turn so the comparison sample stays balanced even mid-conversation.
Because outputs are nondeterministic, canary stages should be shortened so a regression is not masked by soak time.
A golden set of hand-written happy paths is the fastest route to a trustworthy offline score.
questions.explanation: A model can be technically flawless on the infrastructure dashboards and still produce worse reasoning or a tone shift, and nondeterminism means longer soak times rather than shorter ones.

questions.question: Which conclusion does the lesson support?
options: Academic metrics such as perplexity and BLEU score measure task success well enough to be the primary metric.
A golden set has to mirror production traffic patterns, including edge and adversarial cases, and be maintained as production changes.
The eval is the customer, so when the eval and the user disagree you change the model.
Evals should be implemented after the agent ships, once real usage data is available.
questions.explanation: A dataset that does not faithfully reproduce production traffic is a biased design, and an eval is a proxy for the customer, so a disagreement is fixed in the eval.
